page: Microsoft Azure EC64as_cc_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The virtual machine achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, PassMark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory performance is highly polarized: cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth is exceptionally strong at 4138.93 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read and write bandwidths fall into the average tier. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA extensions, yielding strong PassMark encryption scores.

While the server excels at memory-heavy operations and database tasks, showing strong Redis SET operations and PassMark database performance, it exhibits limitations in large-scale machine learning. Text generation for large 70B LLM models is weak, producing only 2.75 tokens per second due to the lack of GPU acceleration. Consequently, this server is best suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and parallel data decompression tasks, rather than heavy AI model inference.
